ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r2.claim: The angel taught the Prophet like an affectionate teacher, approaching and bending over his pupil, and the Prophet fully grasped the instruction rather than hearing unclear distant words.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r2.anchor: The Prophet (sws) fully grasped and understood this instruction

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p10/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p10/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p10/r13.claim: “To His servant” means to God's servant even though God's name was not just stated, because the referent is unmistakable.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p10/r13.anchor: أي إلى عبد الله، وإن لم يجر لاسمه عز وجل ذكر، لأنه لا يلبس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r1.claim: “What He revealed” magnifies the revelation mentioned before it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r1.anchor: تفخيم للوحي الذي أوحي إليه قبل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God revealed to His servant, meaning the Messenger.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r11.anchor: أي الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، قاله ابن عباس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r12.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r12.claim: Another interpretation makes Gabriel the servant to whom revelation was sent.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r13.claim: The unspecified “what He revealed” is a magnifying ambiguity; the known content included the prescription of the prayers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r13.anchor: إبهام على جهة التعظيم والتفخيم، والذي عرف من ذلك فرض الصلوات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r14.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r14.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Gabriel revealed to God's servant Muḥammad what God had revealed to Gabriel, retaining the same unspecified formulation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r14.anchor: وقال الحسن: فأوحى جبريل إلى عبد الله، محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، ما أوحى، كالأول في الإبهام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r15.speaker: ابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r15.claim: Ibn Zayd says Gabriel conveyed to Muḥammad what God had conveyed to Gabriel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r15.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: فأوحى جبريل إلى عبد الله، محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، ما أوحاه الله تعالى إلى جبريل عليه السلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r16.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r16.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the revelation was that Paradise is forbidden to prophets until Muḥammad enters it and to communities until his community enters it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p11/r16.anchor: أوحى إليه أن الجنة محرمة على الأنبياء حتى تدخلها، وعلى الأمم حتى تدخلها أمتك

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.claim: The opening responds to the disbelievers’ claim in 52:33 that the Prophet invented the revelation.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r10.anchor: the opening verses respond to the contention of the disbelievers in 52:33, He has invented it

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.claim: The sūrah is famous for its rhetorical power and the dispute over the meaning of its opening section.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r11.anchor: because of its poetic rhetorical power and the debate that arises

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.speaker: many commentators
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.claim: Many commentators identify the passage as the Prophet’s two visions of Gabriel in his true form, unlike Gabriel’s usual human appearance.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r12.anchor: Many commentators say the passage refers to the Prophet’s two visions of the Archangel Gabriel in his true form

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.speaker: many others
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.claim: Many others read the passage as the Prophet seeing God, by heart alone or by both eye and heart, during the Night Journey and Ascension.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r13.anchor: Many others interpret it as a reference to the Prophet’s vision of God

RAZI-FULL:v28p249#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p249#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p249#2/r1.claim: One reading is that God revealed to Muhammad what He had revealed to Gabriel, either by addressing him that it was revelation or by creating necessary knowledge in him.
RAZI-FULL:v28p249#2/r1.anchor: أوحى إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أوحاه إلى جبريل أي كلمه الله أنه وحي

RAZI-FULL:v28p249#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p249#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p249#2/r2.claim: Another reading is that God gave Gabriel the proof by which he recognized the message to Muhammad as revelation; on this reading mā is a verbal noun, distinguishing an angel from a jinn.
RAZI-FULL:v28p249#2/r2.anchor: أوحى إلى جبريل ما أوحى إلى محمد دليله الذي به يعرف أنه وحي

STUDYQURAN:53:10/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:10/r1.speaker: JJ, Q, Ṭb
STUDYQURAN:53:10/r1.claim: One view is that Gabriel revealed to the Prophet, God's servant, what God had revealed to Gabriel.
STUDYQURAN:53:10/r1.anchor: (JJ, Q, Ṭb), in which case it would be rendered,“Then he revealed to his servant what he revealed”

STUDYQURAN:53:10/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:10/r2.speaker: Q, Ṭb
STUDYQURAN:53:10/r2.claim: A second view is that God revealed the revelation directly to the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:53:10/r2.anchor: that God revealed the revelation directly to the Prophet (Q, Ṭb)

STUDYQURAN:53:10/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:10/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:10/r3.claim: A third view is that God revealed to Gabriel, His servant, what Gabriel later transmitted to the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:53:10/r3.anchor: what Gabriel then transmitted to the Prophet.

STUDYQURAN:53:10/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:10/r4.speaker: JJ, Ṭb
STUDYQURAN:53:10/r4.claim: The revelation's content is left unnamed to honor its exalted status.
STUDYQURAN:53:10/r4.anchor: What is revealed is not mentioned by name out of reverence for its exalted status (JJ, Ṭb).

TAB-FULL:v22p21/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the servant as Muhammad and says his Lord revealed to him what He revealed.
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى} [النجم: 10] قال: «عبده محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أوحى إليه ربه»

TAB-FULL:v22p21/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r2.claim: On the interpretation that God revealed to Muhammad, ma can be a relative pronoun (“what He revealed”) or a verbal noun (“His revelation”).
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r2.anchor: وقد يتوجه على هذا التأويل «ما» لوجهين: أحدهما: أن تكون بمعنى «الذي» فيكون معنى الكلام فأوحى إلى عبده الذي أوحاه إليه ربه والآخر: أن تكون بمعنى المصدر

TAB-FULL:v22p21/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r3.claim: Al-Hasan identifies the servant as Gabriel.
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى} [النجم: 10] ، قال الحسن: «جبريل»

TAB-FULL:v22p21/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r4.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r4.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the revelation came through Gabriel's tongue.
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r4.anchor: عن الربيع، {فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى} [النجم: 10] قال: «على لسان جبريل»

TAB-FULL:v22p21/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says Gabriel revealed to the Messenger what God had revealed to him.
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى} [النجم: 10]

TAB-FULL:v22p21/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r6.claim: Tabari prefers that Gabriel revealed to Muhammad what his Lord revealed: the sura opened by speaking about Muhammad and Gabriel, and nothing signals a shift of subject here.
TAB-FULL:v22p21/r6.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك عندنا بالصواب قول من قال: معنى ذلك: فأوحى جبريل إلى عبده محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

BURSEVI:v9p179/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p179/r13.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p179/r13.claim: Gabriel conveyed to God's servant, meaning the Prophet; 'servant' is an honorific relation, as in the opening of the Night Journey.
BURSEVI:v9p179/r13.anchor: أي جبرائيل {إلى عبده} أي عبد الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v9p179/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p179/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p179/r14.claim: The implicit 'of God' is omitted before the explicit servant because it is obvious, like the implicit earth in the phrase 'on its back' in 35:45.
BURSEVI:v9p179/r14.anchor: وإضماره قبل الذكر لغاية ظهوره كما في قوله تعالى ما ترك على ظهرها من دابة

TABATABAI:53:8-11/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:8-11/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:8-11/r10.claim: If earlier pronouns refer to Gabriel, both occurrences of “revealed” may refer to Gabriel, who revealed to God's servant, the Prophet, what he revealed.

TABATABAI:53:8-11/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:8-11/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:8-11/r11.claim: A reading allows the reference to God without prior mention because God is self-evident.
TABATABAI:53:8-11/r11.anchor: ولا ضير في رجوع الضمير إليه تعالى من عدم سبق الذكر

TABATABAI:53:8-11/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:8-11/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:8-11/r12.claim: Alternatively, all three pronouns refer to God, who revealed through Gabriel to His servant.
TABATABAI:53:8-11/r12.anchor: الضمائر الثلاث لله والمعنى فأوحى الله بتوسط جبريل إلى عبده

TABATABAI:53:8-11/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:8-11/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:8-11/r13.claim: Another construction has the first pronoun refer to Gabriel and the second and third to God: Gabriel conveyed what God revealed to him.
TABATABAI:53:8-11/r13.anchor: الضمير الأول لجبريل والثاني والثالث لله

TABATABAI:53:8-11/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:8-11/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:8-11/r14.claim: If earlier pronouns refer to the Prophet, all three here refer to God; this is more natural than the prior reading, though that is valid.
TABATABAI:53:8-11/r14.anchor: وهذا المعنى أقرب إلى الذهن من المعنى السابق

TABATABAI:53:1-18#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#2/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:53:1-18#2/r1.claim: Imam al-Sadiq traces the authority of each Imam’s hadith back through the Imams to the Prophet, whose hadith is God’s own speech.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#2/r1.anchor: سمعنا أبا عبد الله عليه السلام يقول حديثي حديث أبي وحديث أبي حديث جدي

TABATABAI:53:1-18#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:1-18#2/r8.speaker: تفسير القمي
TABATABAI:53:1-18#2/r8.claim: Tafsir al-Qummi explains the revelation to the Prophet as direct, face-to-face speech.
TABATABAI:53:1-18#2/r8.anchor: في تفسير القمي في قوله تعالى { فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى } قال

TABRISI:53:10/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:10/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABRISI:53:10/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud reports that the Messenger saw Gabriel with six hundred wings; al-Bukhari and Muslim include it in their Sahih collections.
TABRISI:53:10/r5.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أي جبرائيل ع وله ستمائة جناح

TABRISI:53:10/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:10/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:10/r6.claim: God conveyed through Gabriel to Muhammad what He revealed; mā may be a verbal noun or a relative pronoun.
TABRISI:53:10/r6.anchor: فأوحى الله على لسان جبرائيل إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أوحى

TABRISI:53:10/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:10/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:10/r7.claim: Mā may function as a verbal noun or mean 'that which.'
TABRISI:53:10/r7.anchor: وما يحتمل أن تكون مصدرية ويحتمل أن تكون بمعنى الذي

TABRISI:53:10/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:10/r8.speaker: الحسن والربيع وابن زيد وعطاء عن ابن عباس
TABRISI:53:10/r8.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Rabiʿ, Ibn Zayd, and a report from Ibn Abbas through ʿAtaʾ say Gabriel revealed to Muhammad what God had revealed.
TABRISI:53:10/r8.anchor: فأوحى جبرائيل ع إلى عبد الله محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أوحى الله تعالى إليه عن الحسن

TABRISI:53:10/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:10/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:53:10/r9.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the revelation included the passage from 'Did He not find you an orphan' through 'We raised your mention.'
TABRISI:53:10/r9.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير أوحى إليه ألم يجدك يتيما فآوى

TABRISI:53:10/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:10/r10.speaker: غير مسمى
TABRISI:53:10/r10.claim: One view says Paradise is forbidden to prophets until Muhammad enters it and to nations until his community enters it.
TABRISI:53:10/r10.anchor: أوحى إليه أن الجنة محرمة على الأنبياء حتى تدخلها أنت

TABRISI:53:10/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:10/r11.speaker: غير مسمى
TABRISI:53:10/r11.claim: Another view says God revealed secretly to him, as a poem describes a private mystery infused with intimacy and light.
TABRISI:53:10/r11.anchor: أوحى الله إليه سرا بسر وفي ذلك يقول القائل

THALABI:v9p139/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p139/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p139/r6.claim: The author explains that God revealed to His servant Muhammad whatever He revealed.
THALABI:v9p139/r6.anchor: يعني فأوحى الله سبحانه وتعالى إلى عبده محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أوحى

THALABI:v9p139/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p139/r7.speaker: الحسن والربيع وابن زيد
THALABI:v9p139/r7.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Rabi, and Ibn Zayd say Gabriel revealed to the Messenger what his Lord had revealed to him.
THALABI:v9p139/r7.anchor: قال الحسن والربيع وابن زيد: معناه فأوحى جبريل إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أوحى

THALABI:v9p139/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p139/r8.speaker: سعيد
THALABI:v9p139/r8.claim: Saʿid says the revelation included God’s words that He found Muhammad an orphan and raised his remembrance, linking 93:6 and 94:4.
THALABI:v9p139/r8.anchor: قال سعيد: أوحى إليه ألم يجدك يتيما إلى قوله ورفعنا لك ذكرك

THALABI:v9p139/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p139/r9.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v9p139/r9.claim: One view says the revelation declared Paradise forbidden to prophets until Muhammad enters it, and to peoples until his community enters.
THALABI:v9p139/r9.anchor: وقيل: أوحى إليه أن الجنة محرمة على الأنبياء حتى تدخلها، وعلى الأمم حتى تدخلها أمتك

THALABI:v9p139/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p139/r10.speaker: أبو الحسن الثوري
THALABI:v9p139/r10.claim: Abu al-Hasan al-Thawri describes the revelation as an intimate secret communicated secretly, beyond disclosure by speech or writing.
THALABI:v9p139/r10.anchor: وسئل أبو الحسن الثوري عنه فقال: أوحى إليه سرا بسر من سر في سر

THALABI:v9p139/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p139/r11.speaker: الشاعر
THALABI:v9p139/r11.claim: The anonymous poet’s lines portray a secret between lovers, infused with intimacy and bewildering light, illustrating al-Thawri’s gloss.
THALABI:v9p139/r11.anchor: بين المحبين سر ليس يفشيه … قول ولا قلم للخلق يحكيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p21/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p21/r1.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء والكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p21/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, in reports from Ata and al-Kalbi, says Gabriel revealed to Muhammad what God had revealed to Gabriel.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p21/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء والكلبي: أوحى جبريل إلى النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- ما أوحى الله إليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p21/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p21/r2.speaker: قتادة والحسن وابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p21/r2.claim: Qatada's interpretation, also held by al-Hasan and Ibn Zayd and chosen by al-Farra, al-Zajjaj, and Ibn al-Anbari, is that God reveals to Gabriel and Gabriel to Muhammad.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p21/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة: يوحي الله إلى جبريل ويوحي جبريل إلى محمد -صلى الله عليه وسلم-، هذا قول الحسن، وابن زيد

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:9-13/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:9-13/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:9-13/r2.claim: The servant is Muhammad; what was revealed is what God revealed to Gabriel.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:9-13/r2.anchor: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم { ما أوحى } الله عز وجل إلى جبريل عليه السلام

QASHANI:53:10-12/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:53:10-12/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:53:10-12/r1.claim: At the station of unity, God communicated without Gabriel as intermediary secrets that cannot be disclosed to someone in the prophetic office.
QASHANI:53:10-12/r1.anchor: في مقام الوحدة بلا واسطة جبريل عليه السلام

ELMALILI:53:8-10/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r12.claim: The pronoun in “His servant” refers to God in every reading, since God is understood from the preceding discussion even when the strong one is taken as Gabriel.
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r12.anchor: عَبْدِهِۦ’deki zamirin Allah’a râci‘olduğunda ihtilâf yoktur. “Şedîdü’l-kuvâ”dan murad Allah teâlâ olduğuna göre bu zâhirdir.

ELMALILI:53:8-10/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r13.claim: One reading has Gabriel approach and convey each revelation God sent to Muhammad, first appearing in full form to establish its divine origin and then conveying it piecemeal.
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r13.anchor: Cebrâil böyle yaklaştı da Allah’ın kulu Muhammed aleyhisselâm’a gönderdiği her vahyi getirdi, vahyetti onu öyle tâlim etti

ELMALILI:53:8-10/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r14.claim: Elmalili prefers that Muhammad, God's chosen servant, drew near to his Lord after the ascent and received revelation directly, without Gabriel as intermediary.
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r14.anchor: Allah’ın has kulu olan sâhibiniz Muhammed aleyhisselâm o istivâdan sonra Rabbine öyle yaklaştı

ELMALILI:53:8-10/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r15.claim: The well-known direct revelation at the Mi'raj was prayer; another report says no prophet or community will enter Paradise before Muhammad's prophet and community.
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r15.anchor: Bunun birisi namaz olduğu mâruftur, bir de şu rivayet edilmiştir: Peygamberlerden hiçbiri senden evvel cennete girmeyecek

ELMALILI:53:8-10/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r16.speaker: Resûlullah
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r16.claim: Muslim reports that the Prophet received five daily prayers and the closing verses of al-Baqara, and that grave sins were forgiven for community members who did not associate partners with God.
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r16.anchor: Sahîh-i Müslim’de “Resûlullah’a üç şey verildi. Beş vakit namaz verildi, Sûre-i Bakara’nın havâtimi verildi

ELMALILI:53:8-10/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r17.speaker: Nizameddin Nîsâbûrî
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r17.claim: Nishaburi says the revelation's details in that private gathering were apparently secrets, realities, and kinds of knowledge known only to God and His Messenger.
ELMALILI:53:8-10/r17.anchor: Nitekim Nizameddin Nîsâbûrî tefsirinde der ki:

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.claim: The mysterious, vivid scene points to faith about what senses cannot reach and warns against straining reason beyond its limits.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r1.anchor: duyularla algılanamayan, fizik âlemin ötesine taşan konularda imanın esas olduğuna

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.claim: The passage condemns pagan attempts to make divinity concrete through material or spiritual intermediaries and to ascribe godhood to beings besides God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r2.anchor: Allah’tan başka varlıklara tanrılık izâfe etme telakkisini mahkûm etme

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r29.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r29.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r29.claim: If Gabriel is the subject, after approaching he brings and teaches Muhammad the revelations God sent to His servant.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r29.anchor: Bu yaklaşmayı takiben Cebrâil, Allah’ın, kulu Muhammed’e gönderdiği vahiyleri ona getirip öğretti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r30.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r30.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r30.claim: If God is the subject, Muhammad’s nearness removes the intermediaries and God gives revelation directly to His servant.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r30.anchor: Resûlullah rabbine öylesine yaklaştı ki aradaki vasıtalar kalktı ve Allah Teâlâ kuluna vahyini doğrudan doğruya verdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r31.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r31.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r31.claim: If these verses describe the Miʿrāj, the direct-revelation reading is stronger.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r31.anchor: Bu âyetlerde mi‘rac sırasındaki gelişmelerin anlatıldığı kabul edildiği takdirde ikinci yorum daha kuvvetli olmaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r32.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r32.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r32.claim: The commentary also proposes that Gabriel appeared in his true form and approached closely, after which God revealed through Gabriel whatever He willed.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r32.anchor: Cebrâil asıl şekliyle göründü, sonra iyice yaklaştı ve Allah onun aracılığıyla kuluna dilediğini vahyetti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r33.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r33.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r33.claim: If the scene is the Miʿrāj, appearance, horizon, Sidra, descent, and nearness are figurative descriptions of divine acts and attributes, understood without asking how or how much.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r33.anchor: “görünme, yüce ufukta, sidretü’l-müntehâda olma, inme, çok yaklaşma” gibi ifadeleri mecazi mânada almak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r61.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r61.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r61.claim: Elmalılı reads verses 9–10 as Muhammad approaching God so closely after the horizon that every intermediary, even Gabriel, disappeared and God revealed directly to him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:5/r61.anchor: her vasıta ortadan kalktı yani mi‘racda Cebrâil dahi vasıta olmaksızın Allah Teâlâ kuluna

QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r6.claim: God revealed to Muhammad what He revealed.
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r6.anchor: أي أوحى الله إلى محمد ما أوحى

QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r7.claim: One view says God gave Muhammad burdens or secrets that He disclosed to no one else.
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r7.anchor: ويقال : أحمله أحمالا لم يطلع عليها أحد

QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r8.claim: Another view gives the revelation as God's reminders that He sheltered the Prophet as an orphan, guided him, and enriched him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r8.anchor: ويقال : قال له : ألم أجدك يتيما فآويتك ؟ ألم أجدك ضالا فهديتك ؟ ألم أجدك عائلا فأغنيتك

QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r9.claim: Another view says God gave him glad tidings of the Basin and Kawthar.
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r9.anchor: ويقال : بشره بالحوض والكوثر . ويقال : أوحى إليه

QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r10.claim: Another view says Paradise is forbidden to prophets until Muhammad enters it and to nations until his community enters it.
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r10.anchor: ويقال : أوحى إليه أن الجنة محرمة على الأنبياء حتى تدخلها ، وعلى الأمم حتى تدخلها أمتك

QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r11.claim: All those explanations are sound, but there were also other things in the encounter that no one was shown.
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r11.anchor: والأولى أن يقال : هذا الذي قالوه كله حسن ، وغيره مما لم يطلع أحد

QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r12.claim: That night was uniquely Muhammad's: God raised him to an unmatched station, drew him near, and kept their secret from every observer.
QUSHAYRI:v3p248/r12.anchor: إذ رقاه إلى ما رقاه ، ولقاه بما لقاه ، وأدناه حيث لا دنو قبله ولا بعده

SULAMI:v2p284#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p284#3/r1.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p284#3/r1.claim: God revealed directly to the Prophet’s innermost secret and heart, with no intermediary; the only exception mentioned is the later granting of intercession for his community.
SULAMI:v2p284#3/r1.anchor: قال جعفر : ﴿ فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى ﴾ قال بلا واسطة فيما بينه وبين سره إلى قلبه

SULAMI:v2p284#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p284#3/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p284#3/r2.claim: God gave His servant a revelation whose content He kept concealed because it was exclusive to him, while what the Prophet brought to people was made public.
SULAMI:v2p284#3/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه في هذه الآية : ألقى إلى عبده ما القي ولم يظهر ما الذي أرجئ

SULAMI:v2p284#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p284#3/r3.speaker: الصادق
SULAMI:v2p284#3/r3.claim: At the utmost nearness between Beloved and beloved, the Prophet experienced utmost awe, and God met it with utmost gentleness because only utmost gentleness can bear utmost awe.
SULAMI:v2p284#3/r3.anchor: قال الصادق : ^ ( دنى فتدلى * فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى ) ^ . قال : لما قرب الحبيب من الحبيب بغاية القرب نالته غاية الهيبة

SULAMI:v2p284#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p284#3/r4.speaker: الصادق
SULAMI:v2p284#3/r4.claim: The intimate communication was a secret between God and His beloved, known only to the revealer and the recipient.
SULAMI:v2p284#3/r4.anchor: قال الصادق : ^ ( دنى فتدلى * فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى ) ^ . قال : لما قرب الحبيب من الحبيب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r1.claim: Wahy is anything used to indicate something to another, whether writing, gesture, or message.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة : الوحي : كل شيء دللت به من كتاب أو إشارة أو رسالة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r2.claim: Wahy is anything conveyed so that another knows it, however it is conveyed.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r2.anchor: وقال ابن فارس : كل ما ألقيته إلى غيرك حق يعلمه فهو : وحي ، كيف كان

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r3.claim: Wahy can also mean swift or sound; istawḥaynāhum means that we called them to cry out.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r3.anchor: والوحي : السريع . والوحي : الصوت . ويقال : استوحيناهم ، أي : استصرخناهم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r4.speaker: بعضهم
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r4.claim: Some define wahy as conveying an intended meaning to its recipient in the swiftest, gentlest way.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r4.anchor: وقد حد بعضهم الوحي فقال : إيصال المراد إلى الموحى إليه على أسرع وجه وألطفه

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p621/r9.anchor: والخامس : القول . ومنه قوله تعالى في النجم

FARRA:v3p94/r11.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p94/r11.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p94/r11.claim: Gabriel approached Muhammad to within two Arabic bow-lengths or less, then revealed to God's servant, Muhammad.
FARRA:v3p94/r11.anchor: يعنى: جبريل صلى الله عليه، دنا من محمد صلى الله عليه حتى كان قاب قوسين عربيتين

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p428/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p428/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p428/r1.claim: The revelation to His servant was from God.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p428/r1.anchor: {فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى} عن الله عز وجل.

NAHHAS:v4p267/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p267/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v4p267/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies God's servant as Muhammad, yielding the sense that God revealed to Muhammad.
NAHHAS:v4p267/r5.anchor: روى هشام الدستوائي عن قتادة عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس قال عبده محمد

NAHHAS:v4p267/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p267/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
NAHHAS:v4p267/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd and other exegetes take Gabriel as the subject who revealed to Muhammad, God's servant; al-Nahhas prefers this because the surrounding account concerns Gabriel and Muhammad.
NAHHAS:v4p267/r6.anchor: فأوحى جبرائيل إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم عبد الله وهو قول جماعة من أهل التفسير منهم ابن زيد قال وهذا أشبه بسياق الكلام

SAMIN-DURR:53:10/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:10/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:10/r1.claim: The implied subject of فأوحى is God; He was not just mentioned, but the subject is unambiguous.
SAMIN-DURR:53:10/r1.anchor: قوله: { فأوحى }: أي الله، وإن لم يجر له ذكر لعدم اللبس.

SAMIN-DURR:53:10/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:10/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:10/r2.claim: ما أوحى is deliberately left unspecified to magnify the revelation. Ibn Malik uses it to argue that a relative clause need not refer to something already familiar to the listener, as in 20:78; grammarians more commonly require that familiarity.
SAMIN-DURR:53:10/r2.anchor: وقوله: " ما أوحى " أبهم تعظيما له ورفعا من شأنه، وبه استدل جمال الدين ابن مالك

ZAJJAJ:v5p71/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p71/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p71/r1.claim: Gabriel revealed to the Prophet what he revealed.
ZAJJAJ:v5p71/r1.anchor: أي فأوحى جبريل إلى النبي عليه السلام ما أوحى

ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n6/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n6/r1.claim: The phrase alludes both to the angel's exceptional manifestation in true form and to the content of revelation generally.
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n6/r1.anchor: allusion to the exceptional manifestation of the angel "in his true shape and nature"

ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n6/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n6/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n6/r2.claim: Even chosen prophets do not receive the ultimate mysteries of existence, life and death, creation's purpose, or the universe's nature.
ASAD-NOTES:53:10#n6/r2.anchor: even to His chosen prophets God does not entirely unveil the ultimate mysteries of existence, of life and death

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p247/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p247/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p247/r1.claim: Qur'anic oaths perform their proper work of emphasis, affirmation, and solemnity.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p247/r1.anchor: والقسم فيها جميعاً على وجهه من التأكيد والتقرير والإعظام

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p247/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p247/r2.speaker: المفسرون والبلاغيون
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p247/r2.claim: Exegetes and rhetoricians commonly say the oath-waaw magnifies what follows; the author questions this account because created things cannot be measured against the Creator's greatness.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p247/r2.anchor: فإن ذلك يدعو إلى مراجعة لما قنع به المفسرون والبلاغيون في تأويل هذه الواو بأنها لإعظام ما تلاها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p247/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p247/r3.speaker: الفخر الرازي والنيسابورى والطبرسى والشيخ محمد عبده
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p247/r3.claim: The author says philosophical and ishari interpretations by these commentators make the oath-waaw carry meanings it cannot plausibly bear.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p247/r3.anchor: وحمّلوا الآيات من التأويلات الفلسفية والإشارية - في مثل ما نقرأ في تفاسير الفخر الرازي والنبيسابورى والطبرسى والشيخ محمد عبده

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p247/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p247/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p247/r4.claim: The Qur'an points plainly to the benefits of night, day, sun, and moon without an oath, as in passages on light, rest, and reckoning.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p247/r4.anchor: مع ملاحظة أن البيان القرآني يلفت إلى آيتى الليل والنهار، أو الشمس والقمر، بغير القسم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p54/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p54/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p54/r3.claim: ʿAbd refers to body and spirit together, so this wording affirms a bodily as well as spiritual Isra and Mi'raj; otherwise the disbelievers would not have denied the miracle.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p54/r3.anchor: تستخدم كلمة (عبد) على مجموع الجسد والروح وهنا إثبات على أن الإسراء والمعراج كان بالروح والجسد

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.claim: Verses 1–18 establish that the recited Qur'an is not soothsaying or fortune-telling but was revealed to the Prophet by God's trusted, dependable angel.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r7.anchor: not the work of a soothsayer or a fortune-teller

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.claim: The discourse presents every verse as true and inevitable, and rejects the idea that the Prophet's experiences of revelation and Gabriel are illusions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p39/r8.anchor: All its verses are based on the truth and what is stated in them is inevitable

NASHR:v2p408/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p408/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
NASHR:v2p408/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to say the Prophet saw the treasures God would open for his community and was given a thousand paradisal palaces; the report is sound to Ibn Abbas and treated as raised by convention.
NASHR:v2p408/r1.anchor: وهذا إسناد صحيح إلى ابن عباس. ومثل هذا لا يقال: إلا عن توقيف فهو في حكم المرفوع عند الجماعة

NASHR:v2p408/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p408/r2.speaker: السدي عن ابن عباس
NASHR:v2p408/r2.claim: Al-Suddi reports from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet's takbīr expressed distress over the prospect of a member of his household entering Hell.
NASHR:v2p408/r2.anchor: وقال السدي عن ابن عباس كبر - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أن لا يدخل أحد من أهل بيته النار

NASHR:v2p408/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p408/r3.speaker: الحسن وأبو جعفر الباقر
NASHR:v2p408/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Abu Jaʿfar al-Baqir explain the takbīr as referring to the Prophet's intercession.
NASHR:v2p408/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن يعني بذلك الشفاعة، وهكذا قال أبو جعفر الباقر رضي الله عنه

NASHR:v2p408/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p408/r4.speaker: أبو بكر محمد بن إسحاق
NASHR:v2p408/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq, among earlier authorities, says Gabriel revealed this sūra to the Prophet when appearing in his original created form and descending at al-Abṭaḥ.
NASHR:v2p408/r4.anchor: الإمام أبو بكر محمد بن إسحاق أن هذه السورة هي التي أوحاها جبرائيل عليه السلام إلى رسول الله

NASHR:v2p408/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p408/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p408/r5.claim: The author favors the Gabriel-vision explanation: takbīr is usually occasioned by something momentous or frightening.
NASHR:v2p408/r5.anchor: وهذا قول قوي جيد إذ التكبير إنما يكون غالبا لأمر عظيم، أو مهول

NASHR:v2p408/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p408/r6.speaker: مكي وعلي
NASHR:v2p408/r6.claim: Makki says takbīr honors God at Quran recitation and revelation's completion; Ali's instruction to make takbīr at the end of the Mufaṣṣal supports seeing it as gratitude, joy, and a completion signal.
NASHR:v2p408/r6.anchor: وقيل زيادة في تعظيم الله مع التلاوة لكتابه والتبرك بختم وحيه وتنزيله والتنزيه له من السوء قاله مكي

NASHR:v2p408/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p408/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p408/r7.claim: Finding no earlier explanation for takbīr beginning at al-Sharḥ, the author suggests the rule at al-Ḍuḥā's end may carry over to the next sūra's opening.
NASHR:v2p408/r7.anchor: لم أر أحدا تعرض إلى هذا فيحتمل أن يكون الحكم الذي لسورة الضحى انسحب للسورة التي تليها

NASHR:v2p408/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p408/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p408/r8.claim: Alternatively, since al-Sharḥ continues listing blessings bestowed on the Prophet, takbīr may have been delayed until that count of blessings was complete.
NASHR:v2p408/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أنه لما كان ما ذكر فيها من النعم عليه - صلى الله عليه وسلم - هو من تمام تعداد النعم عليه فأخر إلى انتهائه

ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r1.claim: Gabriel is the subject of revealed and God's servant is the Prophet; Allah's name is omitted because its referent is obvious.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r1.anchor: فأوحى ( أي جبريل عليه السلام ( إلى عبده ( أي عبد الله

ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r2.claim: The unmentioned divine subject is common in speech, as in 35:45 and 97:1.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r2.anchor: ومنه ( ولو يؤاخذ الله الناس بما كسبوا ما ترك على ظهرها من دابة ) وقوله سبحانه : ( إنا أنزلناه في ليلة القدر )

ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r3.claim: The object means what Gabriel revealed; Gabriel is the concealed subject, and the content is indefinite for grandeur.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r3.anchor: أي الذي أوحاه والضمير المستتر لجبريل عليه السلام أيضا وإبهام الموحي به للتفخيم

ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r4.speaker: أبو زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r4.claim: Abu Zayd makes the concealed subject God: Gabriel revealed to the Prophet what God revealed to Gabriel.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r4.anchor: الضمير المستتر لله عز وجل أي أوحى جبريل إلى عبد الله ما أوحاه الله إلى جبريل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r5.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r5.claim: Alusi says the first interpretation is transmitted from al-Hasan and is better.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r5.anchor: والأول مروي عن الحسن وهو الأحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r6.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r6.claim: Another view makes both instances of revealed refer to God and identifies the servant as Gabriel; Alusi calls it implausible.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p48#4/r6.anchor: لله تعالى والمراد بالعبد جبريل عليه السلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p402#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p402#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p402#2/r1.claim: God revealed to His servant Muhammad what He revealed.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p402#2/r1.anchor: أي: أوحى الله {إلى عبده} محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أوحى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p402#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p402#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء والكلبي والحسن والربيع وابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p402#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas in Ata's narration, al-Kalbi, al-Hasan, al-Rabi, and Ibn Zayd say Gabriel conveyed what the Lord revealed to the Messenger.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p402#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء، والكلبي، والحسن، والربيع، وابن زيد: معناه: أوحى جبريل إلى رسول الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p402#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p402#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p402#2/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the revelation quoted God's care for Muhammad from finding him an orphan to raising his renown.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p402#2/r3.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير: أوحى إليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p402#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p402#2/r4.speaker: غير مسمى
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p402#2/r4.claim: Another view says Paradise is forbidden to prophets until Muhammad enters it and to nations until his community enters it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p402#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: أوحى إليه: إن الجنة محرمة على الأنبياء حتى تدخلها أنت، وعلى الأمم حتى تدخلها أمتك

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:9-11/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:9-11/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:9-11/r4.claim: On one reading, Gabriel communicated to God's servant, ʿAbd Allāh; the pronoun comes before its explicit referent because he is known.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:9-11/r4.anchor: جبريل عليه السلام. { إلى عبده } عبد الله واضماره قبل الذكر

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:9-11/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:9-11/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:9-11/r5.claim: If Gabriel is the subject, the repetition magnifies what was revealed; alternatively, God is the one revealing it to His servant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:9-11/r5.anchor: جبريل عليه السلام وفيه تفخيم للموحى به أو الله إليه

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:9-11/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:9-11/r6.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:9-11/r6.claim: An alternative takes every pronoun as referring to God, identifying Him as the Mighty in power, as in the cited verse.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:9-11/r6.anchor: وقيل الضمائر كلها لله تعالى وهو المعني بشديد القوى

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:9-11/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:9-11/r7.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:9-11/r7.claim: On that alternative, God's drawing near means raising the Prophet's rank, and ‘hanging down’ means drawing him with all his being to the sacred presence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:9-11/r7.anchor: ودنوه منه برفع مكانته وتدليه جذبه بشراشره إلى جناب القدس

BIQAI-FULL:v7p315/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p315/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p315/r10.claim: God secretly conveyed revelation to His servant, meaning Muhammad; the unexpressed antecedent is clear from al-Shūrā’s account of revelation through a messenger, and suits the hidden mode of speech.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p315/r10.anchor: أي ألقى سرا من كلام الله بسبب هذا القرب , وعقبه بقوله

BIQAI-FULL:v7p315/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p315/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p315/r11.claim: Muhammad alone merits this designation here: he never worshipped anyone but God and worshipped Him at Ḥirāʾ and elsewhere.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p315/r11.anchor: لأنه لم يتعبد قط لأحد غير الله

BIQAI-FULL:v7p315/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p315/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p315/r12.claim: The author tentatively connects this descent with the first revelation at Ḥirāʾ, when Muhammad was frightened, returned trembling, and asked to be covered.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p315/r12.anchor: هذه النزلة - والله أعلم - كانت على هذا التقدير في أول الوحي

BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r1.claim: As an alternative to taking the approach and following verbs as Gabriel’s, the pronouns may refer throughout to God, making “His servant” unambiguous.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r1.anchor: ويمكن لأجل احتمال الضمائر لما يناسبها من الظواهر أن يكون ضمير

BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r2.speaker: أنس
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r2.claim: Al-Bukhari’s Isra report from Anas recounts the Prophet’s chest being opened and filled with faith and wisdom, his ascent through the heavens, and the revelation of fifty prayers, later reduced to five worth ten each.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r2.anchor: روى البخاري في التوحيد في باب { وكلم الله موسى تكليما } عن أنس

BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r3.claim: The author favors reading this report’s approacher as God when joined to a later account from Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq: after creation reaches its limit, God’s approach is beyond comprehension and fitting to His majesty.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r3.anchor: وهو في غاية الحسن إذا جمعته مع ما يأتي في هذا الوجه المنقول عن جعفر الصادق رضي الله عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r4.claim: The language of divine approach and descent represents the easy, gentle transmission reaching Muhammad while he remains connected to the holy realm; it does not assign God a bodily location or likeness.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r4.anchor: فكان الدنو والتدلي تمثيلا لما وصل منه سبحانه إلى عبده محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بغاية السهولة واليسر واللطافة

BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r5.speaker: عثمان بن أبي العاص
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r5.claim: A report in the author’s Juzʾ al-ʿAyshī likens the nightly divine descent and answering of prayers to a king opening doors first to his intimates, then progressively to everyone; the author calls the comparison representational.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r5.anchor: كما رويناه في جزء العيشي من حديث عثمان بن أبي العاص رضي الله عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r6.claim: God is independent of such degrees, has no likeness, and nothing resembles Him; the royal analogy only explains the address in familiar terms.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r6.anchor: وأما من هو غني عن كل شيء فله سبحانه المثل الأعلى

BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r7.claim: The author points to the discussion of Qur’an al-Fajr in al-Isrāʾ for further explanation of this analogy.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p316/r7.anchor: وفي { قرآن الفجر } من سورة سبحان

DURR-FULL:v7p645/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p645/r2.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v7p645/r2.claim: The revelation was from Gabriel to the servant of his Lord.
DURR-FULL:v7p645/r2.anchor: {فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى} جبريل إلى عبد ربه

DURR-FULL:v7p646/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the servant to whom revelation came as Muhammad.
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى} قال: عبده محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v7p646/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r2.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r2.claim: Anas transmits the Prophet's account of seeing the greatest light, screened by a curtain of pearls and rubies, after which God revealed what He willed.
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r2.anchor: عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: رأيت النور الأعظم ولط دوني بحجاب رفرفه الدر والياقوت

DURR-FULL:v7p646/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r3.speaker: سريج بن عبيد
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r3.claim: Surayj reports that when Gabriel sensed the Lord's approach he prostrated and glorified God until God completed what He revealed to His servant.
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r3.anchor: عن سريج بن عبيد قال: لما صعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى السماء فأوحى الله إلى عبده ما أوحى قال: فلما أحس جبريل بدنو الرب خر ساجدا

DURR-FULL:v7p646/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r4.speaker: سريج بن عبيد
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r4.claim: Surayj says Gabriel then raised his head in his created form, with wings adorned with emerald, pearl, and ruby, filling the two horizons between his eyes.
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r4.anchor: ثم رفع رأسه فرأيته في خلقه الذي خلق عليه منظوم أجنحته بالزبرجد واللؤلؤ والياقوت

DURR-FULL:v7p646/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r5.speaker: سريج بن عبيد
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r5.claim: Surayj says Gabriel had previously appeared in varied forms, most often as Dihya al-Kalbi and sometimes as if seen through a sieve.
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r5.anchor: وكنت لا أراه قبل ذلك إلا على صور مختلفة وأكثر ما كنت أراه على صورة دحية الكلبي

DURR-FULL:v7p646/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r6.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r6.claim: Ibn Umar reports that Gabriel used to come to the Prophet in the form of Dihya al-Kalbi.
DURR-FULL:v7p646/r6.anchor: عن ابن عمر أن جبريل كان يأتي النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في صورة دحية الكلبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p98/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p98/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p98/r2.claim: The revelation clause is the point; the preceding stages are a prelude portraying extraordinary events in familiar terms to show revelation is possible despite the polytheists' denial.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p98/r2.anchor: وهذا التفريع هو المقصود من البيان وما قبله تمهيد له ، وتمثيل لأحوال عجيبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p98/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p98/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p98/r3.claim: The subject of awḥā is God, understood from the earlier statement that it is revelation; God revealed to Muhammad, sufficient to refute denial of revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p98/r3.anchor: وضمير { أوحى } عائد إلى الله تعالى المعلوم من قوله : { إن هو إلا وحي يوحى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p98/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p98/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p98/r4.claim: Calling the Prophet ‘His servant’ in place of a pronoun honors him through the special attribution to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p98/r4.anchor: وإيثار التعبير عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعنوان { عبده } إظهار في مقام الإضمار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p98/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p98/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p98/r5.claim: The unspecified content of ‘what He revealed’ magnifies the revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p98/r5.anchor: وفي قوله : { ما أوحى } إبهام لتفخيم ما أوحى إليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the verse to mean that God revealed to His servant Gabriel what He revealed.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198/r6.claim: The unspecified 'what He revealed' is deliberately left vague for magnification; what is known from it is the prescription of prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198/r6.anchor: وفي قوله: ما أوحى إبهام على جهة التفخيم والتعظيم، والذي عرف من ذلك فرض الصلاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198/r7.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says Gabriel revealed to God's servant Muhammad, leaving the content unspecified as in Ibn Abbas's account.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198/r7.anchor: وقال الحسن المعنى: فأوحى جبريل إلى عبد الله محمد ما أوحى كالأولى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198/r8.claim: Ibn Zayd says Gabriel revealed to Muhammad what God had revealed to Gabriel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198/r8.anchor: وقال ابن زيد المعنى: فأوحى جبريل إلى عبد الله محمد ما أوحى الله إلى جبريل.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر ونافع وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir, Asim, and Ibn Amir use fatha at all verse endings; Asim in Abu Bakr's transmission uses imāla on raʾā. Nafi and Abu Amr use an intermediate form; Hamza and al-Kisai use imāla throughout, while Abu Amr in Ubayd's transmission uses it for al-aʿlā and tadallā.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p198#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر هذه السورة كلها بفتح أواخر آيها وأمال عاصم في رواية أبي بكر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p67/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p67/r1.speaker: قائلون بأن ذلك كان ليلة المعراج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p67/r1.claim: One view is that God spoke directly to Muhammad, without an intermediary, during the Night Journey.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p67/r1.anchor: أوحى الله إلى محمد كفاحا بلا واسطة وهذا على قول من يقول إنه كان في ليلة المعراج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p67/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p67/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p67/r2.claim: A report transmitted by ʿAṭāʾ from Ibn ʿAbbās says Gabriel conveyed to the Prophet what God had revealed to him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p67/r2.anchor: أوحى جبريل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أوحى الله إليه رواه عطاء عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p67/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p67/r3.speaker: عائشة والحسن وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p67/r3.claim: Another report, attributed to ʿĀʾisha, al-Ḥasan, and Qatāda, says God revealed to Gabriel what He would reveal.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p67/r3.anchor: أوحى الله إلى جبريل ما يوحيه روي عن عائشة رضي الله عنها والحسن وقتادة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p447/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p447/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p447/r6.claim: The phrase can mean Gabriel revealed to God's servant Muhammad, or God revealed to Muhammad through Gabriel; Ibn Kathir says both meanings are valid.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p447/r6.anchor: فأوحى جبريل إلى عبد الله محمد ما أوحى. أو: فأوحى الله إلى عبده محمد ما أوحى بواسطة جبريل وكلا المعنيين صحيح

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p447/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p447/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p447/r7.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the revelation included reminders that God found Muhammad an orphan and raised his renown.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p447/r7.anchor: وقد ذكر عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {فأوحى إلى عبده ما أوحى} ، قال: أوحى إليه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r1.speaker: غيره
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p448/r1.claim: Another reported view says Paradise is forbidden to prophets until Muhammad enters it, and to nations until his community enters it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports a vision, qualified as probably in sleep, in which God asked about the Highest Assembly's dispute, placed a hand between the Prophet's shoulders, and granted him knowledge of heaven and earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "أتاني ربي الليلة في أحسن صورة -أحسبه يعني في النوم-

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r2.claim: The report names as expiations remaining in mosques after prayer, walking to Friday prayers, and completing ablution despite hardship; it says these bring a good life and death and erase sins.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "أتاني ربي الليلة في أحسن صورة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r3.claim: The Prophet is instructed to ask for good deeds, leaving wrongs, love of the poor, and protection from being caught in a trial.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r3.anchor: وقال: قل يا محمد إذا صليت: اللهم، إني أسألك الخيرات

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r4.claim: The report defines the degrees as feeding others, spreading peace, and praying at night while people sleep.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r4.anchor: والدرجات بذل الطعام، وإفشاء السلام، والصلاة بالليل والناس نيام

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir notes a similar report from Muadh was cited at the end of Surah Sad.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r5.anchor: وقد تقدم في آخر سورة "ص"، عن معاذ نحوه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r6.claim: A second Ibn Abbas version adds that God gave the Prophet undisclosed knowledge and that the verses describe his heart's vision of God; Ibn Kathir grades this chain weak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: "رأيت ربي في أحسن صورة فقال لي: يا محمد، هل تدري فيم يختصم الملأ الأعلى؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p450/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir explicitly grades the chain of the expanded Ibn Abbas report as weak.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود (على ظن محمد)
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.claim: A report tentatively attributed to Ibn Masud says Muhammad saw Gabriel in his form twice: once when requested, when Gabriel filled the horizon, and again on the ascent. Gabriel then returned to his form and prostrated; the great signs were Gabriel's creation. Ahmad transmits it and Ibn Kathir calls it strange.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p454/r7.anchor: قال محمد: أظنه عن ابن مسعود -أنه قال: إن محمدا لم ير جبريل في صورته إلا مرتين

JISHUMI:v9p6633/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r10.claim: Waḥy is privately conveying a meaning to the mind.
JISHUMI:v9p6633/r10.anchor: والوحي: إلقاء المعنى إلى النفس في خفية

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p393/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p393/r9.speaker: عائشة والحسن وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p393/r9.claim: The servant receiving revelation is Gabriel, who received what he would convey to God's Messenger.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p393/r9.anchor: أنه جبريل عليه السلام أوحى إليه ما يوحي إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، قالته عائشة

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p393/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p393/r10.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p393/r10.claim: Alternatively, the servant is Muhammad, to whom revelation came through Gabriel.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p393/r10.anchor: أنه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم أوحي إليه على لسان جبريل ، قاله ابن عباس والسدي

MUQATIL:53:10-15/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:10-15/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:10-15/r1.claim: The servant to whom God revealed is Muhammad.
MUQATIL:53:10-15/r1.anchor: { فأوحى إلى عبده } محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#6/r1.claim: Gabriel is the one who revealed.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#6/r2.claim: The servant is ʿAbd Allāh (Muhammad); his name need not have appeared earlier because he is unambiguous, as in the cited expression “what it left on its back.”
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#6/r2.anchor: ﴿ إلى عبده ﴾ إلى عبدالله وان لم يجر لاسمه ذكر لانه لا يلتبس

NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#6/r3.claim: The repetition magnifies the revelation that was revealed.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#6/r3.anchor: ﴿ ما أوحى ﴾ تفخيم للوحى الذى اوحى اليه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#6/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#6/r4.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#6/r4.claim: One report says he was told that Paradise is forbidden to prophets until Muhammad enters it, and to communities until his community enters.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p188#6/r4.anchor: قيل اوحى اليه ان الجنة محرمة على الانبياء حتى تدخلها وعلى الامم حتى تدخلها امتك

QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r14.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والربيع وغيرهم
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r14.claim: They say God revealed to Gabriel, who was at the distance of two bows or nearer to Muḥammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:6-10/r14.anchor: المعنى أنه لما رأى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من عظمته ما رأى، وهاله ذلك رده الله إلى صورة آدمي حين قرب من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالوحي، وذلك قوله تعالى: { فأوحى إلى عبده } يعني أوحي الله إلى جبريل وكان جبريل { قاب قوسين أو أدنى } قاله ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة والربيع وغيرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r5.claim: The repeated indefinite wording magnifies the revelation; waḥy is a swift casting or communication, as in the expression waḥāʾ waḥāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى: { فأوحى إلى عبده مآ أوحى } تفخيم للوحي الذي أوحى إليه. وتقدم معنى الوحي وهو إلقاء الشيء بسرعة ومنه الوحاء الوحاء

QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r6.claim: The primary explanation is that God revealed to His servant Muḥammad what He revealed.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r6.anchor: والمعنى فأوحى الله تعالى إلى عبده محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أوحى

QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r7.claim: Another view makes Gabriel the one revealing to his servant, Muḥammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r7.anchor: وقيل: المعنى { فأوحى إلى عبده } جبريل عليه السلام «ما أوحى»

QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r8.speaker: الربيع والحسن وابن زيد وقتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r8.claim: Al-Rabīʿ, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Zayd, and Qatāda say God revealed to Gabriel and Gabriel then revealed to Muḥammad.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r8.anchor: وقيل: المعنى فأوحى جبريل إلى عبد الله محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أوحى إليه ربه. قاله الربيع والحسن وابن زيد وقتادة. قال قتادة: أوحى الله إلى جبريل وأوحى جبريل إلى محمد

QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r9.claim: Exegetes differ whether the revelation is intentionally left unspecified, to be believed generally, or is known and explained.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r9.anchor: ثم قيل: هذا الوحي هل هو مبهم؟ لا نطلع عليه نحن وتعبدنا بالإيمان به على الجملة، أو هو معلوم مفسر؟ قولان

QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r10.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr takes the revelation as specified: God reminded Muḥammad that He sheltered him as an orphan, guided him when astray, and enriched him when needy, alongside 94:1–4.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r10.anchor: وبالثاني قال سعيد بن جبير، قال: أوحى الله إلى محمد: ألم أجدك يتيما فآويتك! ألم أجدك ضالا فهديتك! ألم أجدك عائلا فأغنيتك! ألم نشرح لك صدرك * ووضعنا عنك وزرك * الذي أنقض ظهرك * ورفعنا لك ذكرك [الشرح: 1 - 4]

QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r11.claim: Another view says God revealed that Paradise is forbidden to prophets until Muḥammad enters, and to communities until his community enters.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:10/r11.anchor: وقيل: أوحى الله إليه أن الجنة حرام على الأنبياء حتى تدخلها يا محمد، وعلى الأمم حتى تدخلها أمتك
